Something to Sell

Something to Sell

Chapter One

Zachary put the flyer beside Mum’s cup before she could take another sip.

“Twenty,” he said.

Maimuna looked up. “Twenty what?”

“Booths. For children.”

She moved her cup away from the paper.

Across the top, in enormous letters, were the words:

YOUNG IDEAS. BIG POSSIBILITIES.

His school had reserved a section at the county fair. Twenty booths would be available for pupils who wanted to make something and sell it, with an adult helping.

Young entrepreneurs, the flyer called them.

Zachary liked the sound of that.

“What are you planning to sell?” Mum asked.

“That is the problem.”

Dad leaned over her shoulder.

“You draw all the time.”

“I know.”

“And you’re always making things.”

“I know.”

“So you’ve got somewhere to start.”

Zachary imagined nineteen children already having brilliant ideas.

“What if somebody takes all the good things?”

Dad pulled out a chair. “All the good things?”

“You know what I mean.”
